title: Industry guidelines for offensive cyber tools unveiled through international Pall Mall Process
content_md: The United States this week signed on to an international set of industry standards for commercial offensive cyber tools that human rights groups and other advocates wish had been stronger. The Pall Mall Process voluntary industry guidelines for commercial cyber intrusion capabilities (CCICs), such as spyware, are the second step in a U.K.- and France-led initiative, following last year’s code for nations. “Through the Industry Guidelines, we aim to disincentivise irresponsible activity across the market for CCICs; improve transparency for regulators, vendors and customers; and provide clarity for businesses operating both within and peripherally to the industry,” the U.K. and French foreign ministries said after the guidelines were finalized Wednesday. The guidelines have four main pillars: compliance with regulations and norms, due diligence, risk management and monitoring of compliance. They contain recommendations like complying with export controls, creating a risk assessment process, implementing technical controls on access such as encryption and continuously observing who can use the capabilities.
